product: Shipper freight volume across multimodal services: Truckload (Dedicated and Network), Intermodal, Logistics and brokerage, plus the Schneider FreightPower digital marketplace. Q2 2026 revenue excluding fuel surcharge was 1328.3M, up 4 percent year over year (8-K exhibit 2026-07-30).
demand: Both, skewed to price. Q2 2026 Truckload revenue per truck per week was 4162, up 5 percent on Network price and productivity while Dedicated volume fell; Intermodal volume rose but revenue per order fell 2 percent on shorter haul; Logistics revenue rose 11 percent on higher revenue per order with lower brokerage volume (2026-07-30).
pricing_power: Renewed demand softness, spot-rate reversal, purchased-transportation spikes, driver wage inflation and fuel volatility. Q4 2025 fell short on softer volume, spiking third-party carrier costs, customer auto-plant shutdowns and healthcare costs (2026-01-29). Falling used-equipment prices would cut gains on equipment sales.
competition: Mexican cross-border and non-compliant, undercutting trucking has been the low-cost pressure; rail intermodal substitutes for long-haul truckload. Schneider itself expands Mexico intermodal and cites non-compliant capacity exiting, so the substitute is present and being partially removed by regulatory actions (2026-07-30).
market_strategy: CEO Jim Filter 2026-07-30: we remain confident that the enterprise will continue to deliver strong operating leverage, with price momentum expected to build. CFO Darrell Campbell 2026-07-30: FY2026 adjusted diluted EPS 0.90-1.10 and net capex 350-400M. Prior CEO Rourke 2026-01-29 promised another 40M cost savings in 2026.
bull: Q2 2026 adjusted EPS 0.29 beat 0.23 consensus and FY26 guidance was raised to 0.90-1.10 from 0.70-1.00 (8-K 2026-07-30); Truckload OR improved 180bps to 91.8%, with 4 net raises in 90 days.
bear: Price is 31.25 with 21-session momentum -11.0% and 63-session -13.6%; targets were trimmed 2026-07-31 (Citigroup, Susquehanna) and all six 90-day actions are Neutral-rated, so the beat is already discounted.
falsifier: Q3 2026 results (est. 2026-10-29): FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance cut below 0.90, or Truckload operating ratio back above 93.6%, or revenue ex-fuel down year over year.
web_what_changed_30_90d: Last 30d: 350M revolver signed 2026-09-16 (8-K) replacing a 250M facility; Q3 dividend declared 2026-07-27 (8-K 2026-07-29). Last 90d: Jim Filter became CEO 2026-07-01 (8-K 2026-01-28); Q2 2026 beat with FY26 adjusted EPS guidance raised to 0.90-1.10 from 0.70-1.00 (2026-07-30). Post-earnings, several analyst targets were trimmed 2026-07-31.
web_true_now_not_modelled: Q2 2026 Truckload operating ratio improved 180bps to 91.8 percent and adjusted EPS 0.29 beat 0.23 consensus (2026-07-30). Guidance raised 2026-07-30. Management says non-compliant capacity is exiting faster than anticipated. New CEO Jim Filter effective 2026-07-01 plus a 350M revolver (2026-09-16). Analyst mean target 34.69 versus 31.20 price (MarketBeat 2026-09-27).
web_demand_product: Shipper freight volume across multimodal services: Truckload (Dedicated and Network), Intermodal, Logistics and brokerage, plus the Schneider FreightPower digital marketplace. Q2 2026 revenue excluding fuel surcharge was 1328.3M, up 4 percent year over year (8-K exhibit 2026-07-30).
web_price_volume_mix: Both, skewed to price. Q2 2026 Truckload revenue per truck per week was 4162, up 5 percent on Network price and productivity while Dedicated volume fell; Intermodal volume rose but revenue per order fell 2 percent on shorter haul; Logistics revenue rose 11 percent on higher revenue per order with lower brokerage volume (2026-07-30).
web_bottleneck: Driver capacity and freight demand are the swing factors; management said H2 2026 guidance spans a range of demand and driver-capacity outcomes (2026-07-30). Schneider relieves shippers capacity and freight-coordination bottlenecks, and launched an MLS CDL training program to ease driver entry (stocktitan 2026-09).
web_who_benefits_next: Second and third order: railroads and intermodal partners, owner-operators leasing via Schneider Finance, third-party carriers on FreightPower, used-truck buyers as gains on equipment sales rise, and dedicated customers wanting guaranteed capacity as industry capacity exits (8-K 2026-07-30).
web_who_loses: Higher-cost and non-compliant carriers and small brokers get squeezed as capacity exits and contract rates firm; brokers competing on price lose share as Schneider Logistics scales (Q2 2026 Logistics operating ratio 96.8 percent, 2026-07-30). Shippers face firmer pricing.
web_margin_collapse_risk: Renewed demand softness, spot-rate reversal, purchased-transportation spikes, driver wage inflation and fuel volatility. Q4 2025 fell short on softer volume, spiking third-party carrier costs, customer auto-plant shutdowns and healthcare costs (2026-01-29). Falling used-equipment prices would cut gains on equipment sales.
web_low_cost_substitute: Mexican cross-border and non-compliant, undercutting trucking has been the low-cost pressure; rail intermodal substitutes for long-haul truckload. Schneider itself expands Mexico intermodal and cites non-compliant capacity exiting, so the substitute is present and being partially removed by regulatory actions (2026-07-30).
web_ceo_promised: CEO Jim Filter 2026-07-30: we remain confident that the enterprise will continue to deliver strong operating leverage, with price momentum expected to build. CFO Darrell Campbell 2026-07-30: FY2026 adjusted diluted EPS 0.90-1.10 and net capex 350-400M. Prior CEO Rourke 2026-01-29 promised another 40M cost savings in 2026.
web_did_they_deliver: Yes so far. FY2025 cost-savings target achieved per CFO (2026-01-29). Q1 2026 was in line at EPS 0.12, and Q2 2026 beat with adjusted EPS 0.29 versus 0.23 consensus, guidance raised (2026-07-30). Succession delivered as promised: Filter became CEO 2026-07-01 (8-K 2026-01-28).
web_what_would_falsify: Q3 2026 results, estimated 2026-10-29, would falsify the thesis if the FY2026 adjusted diluted EPS path to 0.90-1.10 is cut, if Truckload operating ratio rises back above 93.6 percent, or if revenue excluding fuel surcharge declines year over year with softening spot rates (baseline 8-K 2026-07-30).
